shrink-0 gap-12"><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-bold w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp:2;line-clamp:2;font-size:20px;line-height:28px;--typography-color:var(--smoke_coal)">Sales Pitch: How to Write One (With Examples)</span><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-regular w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp: 2; font-size: 15px; line-height: 23px; --typography-color: var(--primaryText);">A sales pitch is a short, prepared message that shows a specific buyer how you solve a problem they already have, and asks for one clear next step. The best pitches are about the buyer, not the product. Most follow the same five parts: a relevant opener, the problem, your solution, proof that it works, and a small ask. Below you'll find that structure, how to write a sales pitch step by step, the main types of pitch, nine sales pitch examples you can adapt, and a fill-in template. What is a sales pitch? A sales pitch is a planned message, spoken or written, that explains why a specific person should take the next step with you. It names a problem the buyer cares about, shows how you fix it, gives a reason to believe you, and ends with one low-effort ask, such as a 15-minute call. It is a conversation starter, not a full presentation. That last point matters. A pitch rarely closes a deal on its own. Its job is to earn the next conversation. If your pitch tries to cover every feature, price and case study at once, the buyer has nothing left to ask about and no reason to reply. The structure of a good sales pitch Almost every pitch that works, whether it's a cold email or a two-minute talk at an event, follows these five parts. Keep the proof honest. A real customer result, a named client (with permission) or a short demo beats a big claim every time. If you don't have a result yet, offer a trial or a sample instead of inventing a number. How to write a sales pitch in 6 steps 1. Pick one buyer and one problem A pitch written for everyone persuades no one. Before you write a word, decide who exactly you're talking to (role, company size, situation) and the single problem you'll lead with. A finance director and an office manager at the same company need different pitches, even for the same product. 2. Research before you write Spend five minutes on the person and their company. Check their profile, recent posts, company news, job openings and the tools they already use. Job openings are a strong signal: a company hiring three new sales reps probably has an onboarding or pipeline problem worth talking about. This is where a professional networking platform helps. When you're connected with people in your target industry, you see their updates, job changes and company news without digging. You can connect with professionals and recruiters on Lobox to keep that research close at hand. 3. Open with them, not you Your first line decides whether the rest gets read. Skip "My name is" and "I'm reaching out because". Open with something about their world: a recent change, a shared connection, or a problem common to their role. Weak: "Hi, I'm Sam from BrightDesk, a leading helpdesk platform." Better: "Your support team posted three job openings this month. That usually means tickets are piling up." 4. Show the change, then prove it Buyers don't buy features. They buy the difference between how things work now and how they could work. Describe that change in one or two sentences, then back it up with one piece of proof. One strong proof point is more convincing than five weak ones. 5. Ask for one small next step End with a single ask that's easy to say yes to. "Can we do a 15-minute call on Tuesday or Wednesday?" works better than "Let me know your thoughts" or "Would you like to buy?" Give a specific action and, where you can, a specific time. 6. Cut it, then say it out loud Read your pitch aloud. If you run out of breath, it's too long. Delete any sentence the buyer wouldn't miss, any adjective that doesn't add meaning, and any line that talks about your company instead of their problem. Most first drafts get better when you cut them by a third. Types of sales pitch The structure stays the same, but the length and tone change with the channel. Here are the main types and when to use each. The word counts and timings above are working guidelines from common sales practice, not hard rules. Test what gets replies in your market. Sales pitch examples Every example below is original and uses made-up companies. Swap in your own product, buyer and real proof. Where a result would go, you'll see [X] so you can add a genuine number. Example 1: Cold email pitch (B2B software) Subject: Faster invoice approvals at Hartley Foods Hi Priya, Congrats on Hartley's new Chicago site. Adding a location usually means more invoices and more people who need to approve them. LedgerLoop routes each invoice to the right approver automatically and flags anything that's overdue. A food distributor about your size cut approval time from [X] days to [Y]. Worth a 15-minute call next Tuesday to see if it fits? Thanks, Marcus Why it works: the opener is specific to Priya, the problem follows naturally from it, there's one proof point and one ask. It's under 90 words. Example 2: Cold call pitch "Hi Daniel, it's Lena from FleetTrack. I'll be quick. I work with regional delivery companies that are losing time to missed routes and fuel overspend. Is that something your team deals with, or is it under control?" Why it works: it's honest about being a cold call, names the problem in one line, and ends with a question so Daniel talks next. A cold call pitch should open a conversation, not deliver a monologue. Example 3: Elevator pitch at a networking event "I run a small bookkeeping firm for restaurants. Most owners I meet are doing their books at midnight after close, and they still get surprised at tax time. We handle the monthly books and send a one-page summary, so they always know where they stand. Who handles the numbers for your place right now?" Why it works: it describes the buyer, the pain and the change in under 30 seconds, then turns it into a conversation. No jargon, no job title to decode. Example 4: Follow-up pitch after no reply Hi Priya, Following up on my note about invoice approvals. I put together a two-minute video showing how the approval flow would look for a business with two sites like Hartley's: [link] If timing's wrong, just say so and I'll check back next quarter. Why it works: it adds something new (a tailored video) instead of "just checking in", and gives an easy way to say no. That respect often gets a reply. Example 5: Social message pitch "Hi Tom, enjoyed your post on hiring for seasonal peaks. We help retail teams schedule part-time staff without the spreadsheet chaos. No pitch deck, just curious: how are you handling the holiday rota this year?" Why it works: it references something Tom actually wrote and asks a real question. On professional networks, a short, human message gets further than a pasted sales email. Example 6: Problem-solution pitch in a meeting "From what you said, the real issue isn't finding leads. It's that your reps spend most of Monday updating the CRM instead of calling. Here's what changes with us: call notes and next steps log themselves after each call. In a pilot with a team like yours, reps got back about [X] hours a week. Would it help to run a two-week pilot with three of your reps?" Why it works: it repeats the buyer's own problem back to them first, which proves you listened, then ties the solution and the ask directly to it. Example 7: Local small business pitch "Hi Rachel, I'm Joe from Clearview Cleaning. I noticed your office is in the Pinewood building. We already clean two other offices there, so we're on site most evenings. I'd love to give you a free quote for weekly cleaning. Could I stop by for ten minutes on Thursday?" Why it works: the proof is local and real (other clients in the same building), and the ask is small and concrete. Small business pitches win on trust and convenience more than features. Example 8: Recruiter pitching a role to a passive candidate Recruiting is selling too. A candidate who isn't job hunting needs a reason to listen, just like a buyer. "Hi Aisha, your work leading the payments app redesign at Novabank caught my eye. I'm hiring a senior product designer for a fintech team that's rebuilding its mobile app from scratch, so you'd shape the product, not polish an old one. It's fully remote and the range is [salary range]. Open to a 15-minute chat this week, even if you're happy where you are?" Why it works: it opens with her actual work, explains what's different about the role, shares the salary range up front and lowers the pressure with "even if you're happy where you are". If you hire, see our guide on how to hire employees for a small business for the steps around the pitch. Example 9: Pitching yourself in a sales job interview Many sales interviews include a version of "sell me this pen" or "pitch me our product". Interviewers aren't checking your script. They want to see if you ask questions before you pitch. The same idea applies on paper: when you write a cover letter, you're pitching yourself to one reader with one problem to solve. "Before I tell you about the pen, can I ask how you use one day to day? ... So you sign a lot of contracts in client meetings, and a cheap pen that skips looks bad in front of a client. This one writes smoothly the first time, every time, and it looks professional on the table. If I could get you a box of ten by Friday, would that work for your team?" Why it works: it uses the same five parts: a question as the opener, the problem in the interviewer's words, the solution, a reason to believe it, and a clear ask. For more on preparing, read our job interview tips. Sales pitch template Copy this, fill in the brackets and cut anything that doesn't apply. Hi [first name], [Opener: one specific thing about them or their company, such as a recent change, post, hire or shared connection.] [Problem: "Teams like yours often ___ when ___."] [Solution: "We help [type of company] [result] by [how, in plain words]."] [Proof: one real result, client name or short demo verify.] [Ask: "Worth a [15-minute call] on [day] or [day]?"] [Your name] Before you send it, check three things: is the first line about them, is there only one ask, and could you say the whole thing in under 30 seconds? Common sales pitch mistakes and how to fix them How long should a sales pitch be? A sales pitch should be as short as it can be while still covering the buyer's problem, your solution, one proof point and an ask. In practice that means roughly 50 to 125 words for a cold email, about 30 seconds for a cold call opener or elevator pitch, and longer only in a booked meeting where the buyer expects detail. If you're unsure, go shorter. A buyer who's interested will ask for more. A buyer who's overloaded will skip a long message entirely. What makes a sales pitch effective? An effective sales pitch is specific to one buyer, focused on a problem they already feel, honest in its proof and easy to respond to. It sounds like a person talking, not a brochure. The biggest difference between pitches that get replies and ones that don't is usually the first line: it either shows you understand the buyer or it doesn't. Keep improving your pitch Treat every pitch as a test. Track which openers get replies, which asks turn into meetings and where conversations stall, then rewrite. Pitches get better through repetition, not through one perfect draft. Have a pitch line that always works for you, or one that flopped badly? Share it in the comments. We'd like to hear what's working in your market. Whether you're building a sales career or hiring a sales team, a strong network makes every pitch easier. Join Lobox to connect with professionals, recruiters and businesses in your industry. FAQ 1.What is an example of a sales pitch? Here's a simple example of a sales pitch for a cold email: "Congrats on opening your second site. More locations usually mean more invoices to approve. We route each invoice to the right person automatically. Worth a 15-minute call on Tuesday?" It opens with the buyer, names a problem, offers a fix and ends with one small ask. 2.What are the 5 parts of a sales pitch? The five parts are an opener that shows you know the buyer, the problem they face, your solution in plain words, proof that it works, and a clear ask for the next step. You can use the same five parts in an email, a phone call, an event conversation or a meeting. Only the length changes. 3.How do you start a sales pitch? Start with something about the buyer, not yourself. A recent company change, a post they wrote, a job they're hiring for or a shared connection all work. Avoid opening with your name, your company's history or "I'm reaching out because". The first line should give them a reason to read the second. 4.How do you end a sales pitch? End with one specific, low-effort ask, ideally with a time attached, such as "Could we do 15 minutes on Thursday?" Avoid vague endings like "let me know your thoughts", which leave the buyer to decide what to do. If it's a follow-up, give them an easy way to say not now. 5. What is the difference between a sales pitch and an elevator pitch? An elevator pitch is one type of sales pitch. It's a 30 to 60 second spoken introduction, usually at an event or first meeting, meant to spark interest. A sales pitch is the broader term and covers cold emails, calls, follow-ups and full meeting presentations aimed at moving a specific buyer forward. 6. How do you answer "sell me this pen" in an interview? Don't start describing the pen. Ask the interviewer a question or two about how they use pens, then pitch back to what they told you: their problem, how this pen solves it, why they can trust that, and a clear ask to close. Interviewers want to see you listen before you sell.</span></div></div><div class="Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__container Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__dirRow w-full style="font-size:15px;line-height:18px;--typography-color:var(--brand)">Trending</span></div></div><div style="height: 114px;" class="Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__container w-full shrink-0 gap-12"><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-bold w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp:2;line-clamp:2;font-size:20px;line-height:28px;--typography-color:var(--smoke_coal)">AI Recruiting: What It Can and Cannot Do for Hiring</span><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-regular w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp: 2; font-size: 15px; line-height: 23px; --typography-color: var(--primaryText);">AI Recruiting: What It Can and Cannot Do for Your Hiring AI recruiting is the use of AI software to handle parts of hiring: finding candidates, screening resumes, drafting job posts and messages, scheduling interviews and answering applicant questions. It's good at fast, repetitive work at volume. It's weak at judgment and context, and it can repeat bias from past data. Use it to cut admin time, and keep a person making every hiring decision. This guide is for owners and hiring managers who don't have a full recruiting team. You'll see what AI handles well, where it falls short, whether it's worth paying for at your hiring volume, and what to ask a vendor before you sign. What is AI recruiting? AI recruiting means using AI-powered software anywhere in the hiring process, from sourcing and screening to scheduling and candidate messages. The software reads resumes, profiles and job requirements, spots patterns, then sorts, ranks, drafts or replies faster than a person can. It supports the people hiring. It doesn't replace the person who decides who gets the job. Most of what you'll come across fits one of three groups: • AI features inside software you already use, such as an applicant tracking system (ATS), a job board or an HR platform • Standalone AI recruiting tools built for one job, like sourcing, screening or scheduling • General AI assistants you prompt yourself, mostly for writing job posts, emails and interview questions One warning: "AI-powered" covers everything from a basic keyword filter to software that ranks candidates on its own. When a vendor says AI, ask what the feature actually does and what it decides. What an AI recruiting tool can do well An AI recruiting tool is most useful on high-volume, repeatable tasks: drafting job posts and outreach, searching large candidate pools, sorting applications against clear requirements, booking interviews and answering routine applicant questions. The common thread is speed on work with clear rules. Anything that needs judgment about a person still needs you. AI recruiting assistant: the admin layer An AI recruiting assistant usually handles coordination: booking interviews, sending reminders, updating candidates on where they stand and drafting follow-ups. For a small team, this is where you get the most time back with the least risk, because the tool isn't deciding who moves forward. If you only try one thing, try this. Candidates also notice it. A same-day reply with three interview slots feels very different from a week of silence. Sourcing and matching Matching tools compare a candidate's skills and experience with what your job asks for, across far more profiles than you could read. They're fast. But they only look for what you tell them to, using the words people happen to put on their profiles. Someone who describes the same skill in different words can slip off the list. That's why sourcing shouldn't start and end inside one tool. Referrals and your own network still find people that ranking misses. Posting your role and connecting with professionals directly on a platform like Lobox widens the pool before any filter touches it. What AI recruiting cannot do AI recruiting cannot judge whether someone will do well in your team, spot potential in people with unusual backgrounds, guarantee fair results or carry legal responsibility for your decisions. It can't fix a vague job description or convince a strong candidate to choose you. Those parts of hiring stay with you. It can't judge fit or potential AI ranks people by how closely their resume matches the job and how similar they look to past patterns. That works against career changers, people returning to work and anyone self-taught. Take a former teacher applying for a training coordinator role. Her resume says "lesson planning" and "classroom management", not "instructional design" or "learning programs". A keyword match ranks her low. A person reading it sees someone who has designed and delivered training every working day for years. It can't guarantee fair outcomes AI learns from data. If your past hires leaned one way, by age, gender or background, a tool trained on that history can learn the same lean and repeat it at scale. Amazon reportedly dropped an experimental resume-screening tool after finding it marked down resumes linked to women Courts are now looking at the software itself. In Mobley v. Workday, filed in 2023, a job applicant alleged that Workday's screening technology discriminated on the basis of age, race and disability. In June 2026 a federal judge refused Workday's request to dismiss the California state-law claims (SHRM). The case hasn't been decided, but the message for employers is clear: "the software made the call" won't protect you. It can't keep you compliant on its own The rules depend on where you hire. Two US examples: • New York City: Local Law 144 covers automated employment decision tools. Employers using one need an independent bias audit every year, must publish a summary of the results and must tell candidates who live in the city that a tool is being used (NYC DCWP FAQ). • Colorado: a new law, SB 26-189, replaced the state's 2024 AI Act. It focuses on notice, disclosure, recordkeeping and human review, and takes effect January 1, 2027 (Proskauer). Federal anti-discrimination law applies whether or not a tool is involved. This isn't legal advice. If you hire in several states, check with an employment lawyer before you switch on automated screening. It can't fix a bad job description If your requirements are wrong or padded, AI filters on the wrong things, just faster. Ten "required" items that are really nice-to-haves will screen out good people at scale. Get the role right first with a clear job description, then let a tool sort against it. It can't build the relationship Candidates are choosing you too, and the best ones usually have options. A real conversation with the hiring manager does more to win someone over than a perfectly timed automated email. Use AI to clear the admin so you have time for those conversations. Is AI recruiting worth it for a small business? It's worth it when you get more applications than you can read properly, or you hire for the same role again and again. If you hire a handful of people a year and can read every application yourself, a paid tool usually costs more in money and setup than it saves. Start with the AI features already built into tools you use. For the full process around these decisions, see our guide on how to hire employees for a small business. How to use AI in recruiting without losing control 1. Start with the lowest-risk tasks. Drafting and scheduling first. Screening last, once you trust your criteria. 2. Write your criteria before any screening. Split must-haves from nice-to-haves. A tool can only be as clear as you are. 3. Keep a person on every rejection. If that's not realistic, review a sample of the AI's rejects every week. 4. Tell candidates when AI is involved. Some places require it, and it builds trust everywhere. 5. Run structured interviews. Ask every candidate the same core questions so an AI summary never becomes the decision. Our list of interview questions to ask candidates gives you a ready set. 6. Check the results. After a few hires, compare who the tool ranked highly with who actually did well. If they don't line up, change the criteria or drop the tool. Questions to ask before you buy an AI recruiting tool Use this checklist on any demo call: ☐ What exactly does the AI do, and what does it decide or recommend? ☐ Can I see why a candidate was ranked high or low? ☐ Can I switch off automatic rejections? ☐ Has the tool had an independent bias audit, and can I see the summary? ☐ Does it use my candidates' data to train its models? ☐ Where is candidate data stored, and what happens to it if I cancel? ☐ Does it support the candidate notices required where I hire? ☐ What does it cost at my hiring volume, not the vendor's typical customer's? For the wider buying process, including features and pricing models, read how to choose recruitment software. AI recruiting chatbots: helpful or annoying? An AI recruiting chatbot answers applicant questions at any hour: what the role pays, where it's based, what happens next. Done well, it saves candidates from waiting days for a simple answer. Done badly, it traps people in loops and makes your company feel cold. Three rules keep it on the helpful side: • Always offer an easy way to reach a person • Only let it give answers you've approved • Never let it reject anyone Where to start this week Pick one admin task that eats your time, such as scheduling or first-draft job posts, and try AI there. Keep screening and decisions in human hands until you've seen how the tool behaves with your roles. Hiring now? Post your role and connect with professionals and recruiters on Lobox, so your shortlist starts with real people, not just a ranking. FAQ Will AI replace recruiters? No. AI takes over repetitive parts of the job, like scheduling, first-pass sorting and drafting messages. It doesn't replace judging people, building relationships with candidates or negotiating offers. The recruiter's job shifts toward those human parts. For small businesses, the realistic gain is getting a few hours back each week, not removing anyone from the hiring process. Is it legal to use AI to screen resumes? In the US, generally yes, but you stay responsible for the outcome. Anti-discrimination law applies whether a person or software makes the screen. Some places add rules: New York City requires an annual independent bias audit and candidate notices, and Colorado's new law takes effect in January 2027. Check the rules where your candidates live before automating any screening. What is an AI recruiting chatbot? It's an automated assistant on your careers page or job ad that answers applicant questions, collects basic details and books interviews. It's useful for routine questions candidates would otherwise wait days to get answered. Keep its answers approved, give people a clear way to reach a human, and don't let it make rejection decisions. Can AI recruiting tools be biased? Yes. A tool trained on past hiring data can learn the patterns in that data, including unfair ones, and repeat them across every application. Bias can also come from how you set the criteria. Ask vendors for independent bias audit results, review a sample of rejected candidates yourself and compare the tool's rankings with how hires actually perform. How much do AI recruiting tools cost? Pricing varies widely. Some charge per user, some per job posting, some per hire, and many AI features come bundled inside an ATS or HR platform you may already pay for. Ask for a quote based on your actual hiring volume, check what's included in the base plan, and try any built-in features before buying a separate tool. Do candidates know when AI screens them? Not always. Unless a law requires notice, many employers don't say. That's changing: New York City already requires employers to notify candidates who live in the city, and Colorado's law focuses on disclosure and notice. Telling candidates up front, even where it isn't required, is the simplest way to avoid looking like you're hiding something.</span></div></div><div class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__truncate index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-regular min-w-0" style="font-size:14px;line-height:18px;--typography-color:var(--secondaryDisabledText)">Automotive</span></div><div class="Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__container Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__dirRow shrink-0 items-center gap-4"><span class="Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__container"><svg width="16" height="16" style="display:inline-block;vertical-align:middle;--icon-color:#5384EE" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><use href="/assets/icons/icon-sprite.svg?v=2b58b27b0f#icon-trend"></use></svg></span><span style="font-size:15px;line-height:18px;--typography-color:var(--brand)">Trending</span></div></div><div style="height: 114px;" class="Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__container w-full shrink-0 gap-12"><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-bold w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp:2;line-clamp:2;font-size:20px;line-height:28px;--typography-color:var(--smoke_coal)">Lif eksikliği vücudumuzda hangi sorunlara yol açıyor?</span><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-regular w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp: 2; font-size: 15px; line-height: 23px; --typography-color: var(--primaryText);">Bazen günün telaşı içinde ne yediğimize değil, yalnızca karnımızın doyup doymadığına odaklanırız. Oysa bedenimizin ihtiyaçları, açlık hissinin çok daha ötesine uzanır. Sabah kahvaltısında beyaz ekmek, öğle yemeğinde az sebzeli bir tabak, akşam ise hızlıca hazırlanmış bir öğün... İlk bakışta bu beslenme düzeni sıradan görünebilir ancak burada gözden kaçan çok önemli bir ayrıntı var. O da lif eksikliği... Sağlıklı bir sindirim sisteminin vazgeçilmez parçalarından biri olan lif, bağırsak hareketlerinden kan şekeri dengesine, tokluk hissinden kalp sağlığına kadar pek çok süreci destekler. Yeterli lif tüketilmediğinde ise bedenin doğal işleyişi bundan etkilenebilir. Üstelik bu etki yalnızca kabızlıkla sınırlı değildir. Peki, sindiremediğimiz bu besin bileşenleri vücudumuzda nasıl bu kadar büyük bir fark yaratabiliyor? Daha önce bu sorunun yanıtını hiç düşünmediyseniz, liflerin vücudumuzdaki şaşırtıcı etkilerini keşfetmeye hazır olun. Çünkü liflerin hikâyesi, sindirimden çok daha fazlasını anlatıyor. LİF EKSİKLİĞİNİN SİNDİRİME ETKİSİ Lif tüketiminin yetersiz olduğu bir beslenme düzeninde ilk fark edilen değişikliklerden biri bağırsak alışkanlıklarında ortaya çıkabilir. Özellikle dışkının hacmini artıran ve bağırsak hareketlerini destekleyen çözünmeyen liflerin az alınması, dışkılamanın zorlaşmasına ve kabızlığa zemin hazırlayabilir. Bu nedenle yulaf, baklagiller, sebzeler, meyveler ve tam tahıllar beslenmenin önemli parçalarıdır. Ancak lifin bağırsaklara katkısı yalnızca sindirimi kolaylaştırmakla bitmez. Çözünür lifler, suyla birleşerek jel benzeri bir yapı oluşturur ve bağırsaklarda yararlı bakteriler tarafından fermente edilebilir. Bu süreçte ortaya çıkan kısa zincirli yağ asitleri, bağırsak hücrelerinin beslenmesine ve bağırsak ortamının desteklenmesine katkıda bulunur. Dolayısıyla liften yoksun bir beslenme, bağırsak mikrobiyotasının ihtiyaç duyduğu besin kaynaklarını da azaltabilir. Kısacası bağırsakların düzenli çalışması için yalnızca ne kadar yemek yediğimiz değil, tabağımızda hangi besinlerin bulunduğu da önem taşır. LİF METABOLİZMAMIZI NASIL ETKİLİYOR? Yemekten kısa süre sonra yeniden acıkmak, gün içinde sık sık atıştırma ihtiyacı hissetmek... Bu durumun tek nedeni lif eksikliği olmasa da liften fakir öğünler, tokluk kontrolünü zorlaştırabilir. Çünkü özellikle çözünür lifler, mide boşalmasını yavaşlatarak sindirim sürecinin daha uzun sürmesine ve tokluk hissinin desteklenmesine yardımcı olur. Lifin metabolik sağlık üzerindeki etkisi de burada devreye girer. Çözünür lifler, karbonhidratların sindirim ve emilim hızını yavaşlatarak yemek sonrasında kan şekerinin daha dengeli yükselmesine katkı sağlayabilir. Yulaf, kuru baklagiller, elma, armut gibi meyveler ve sebzeler, bu açıdan iyi seçeneklerdir. Bazı lif türleri ise kolesterol metabolizmasını destekleyerek LDL kolesterol seviyelerinin düşürülmesine yardımcı olabilir. Bu nedenle yeterli lif tüketimi; kan şekeri kontrolü, kalp-damar sağlığı ve sağlıklı vücut ağırlığının korunması açısından değerli bir beslenme alışkanlığıdır. Elbette lif tek başına kilo verdiren veya metabolik hastalıkları önleyen bir çözüm değildir. Ancak dengeli beslenmenin önemli bir parçası olarak uzun vadeli sağlığa katkı sunar. Lif tüketimini artırmak için karmaşık beslenme programlarına ya da ulaşılması zor gıdalara ihtiyacımız yok. Mutfağımızda zaten bulunan pek çok besin, günlük lif ihtiyacını karşılamaya yardımcı olabilir. Kuru fasulye, nohut, mercimek ve barbunya gibi baklagiller, yulaf, bulgur, tam buğday ekmeği ve tam tahıllı makarnalar, elma, armut, portakal gibi meyveler ile brokoli, enginar, havuç ve kabak gibi sebzeler iyi lif kaynaklarıdır. Ceviz, badem, chia ve keten tohumu da öğünlere lif desteği eklemek için değerlendirilebilir. Örneğin sabah kahvaltısında beyaz ekmek yerine tam tahıllı ekmek tercih etmek, ara öğünde meyveyi kabuğuyla tüketmek, öğle yemeğine mercimekli bir salata eklemek ve akşam yemeğinde bulgur pilavına yer vermek günlük alımı artırabilir. Burada önemli olan tek bir besine yüklenmek yerine farklı lif kaynaklarını gün içine dengeli biçimde dağıtmaktır. BAĞIRSAK SAĞLIĞINIZ İÇİN TABAĞINIZI YENİDEN KEŞFEDİN Lif bakımından zengin beslenmeye geçişte en doğru yaklaşım, büyük değişiklikler yapmak yerine küçük ve sürdürülebilir adımlar atmaktır. Örneğin kahvaltıda yulaf, yoğurt, elma ve birkaç ceviz, öğle yemeğinde zeytinyağlı sebze yemeği, bulgur pilavı ve mercimekli salata, ara öğünde bir armut ve badem ve akşam yemeğinde ise sebze çorbası, nohut yemeği ve tam tahıllı ekmek tercih edilebilir. Böyle bir menü, lif kaynaklarını farklı öğünlere yaymak için fikir verebilir. Ancak porsiyonlar ve toplam lif miktarı kişinin enerji ihtiyacına göre düzenlenmelidir. Bir diğer önemli nokta da lif miktarını aniden artırmamaktır. Çünkü hızlı artış vücudunuzda gaz, şişkinlik ve karın kramplarına yol açabilir. Bu nedenle lif alımını kademeli artırmak ve yeterli sıvı tüketmek gerekir. Özellikle bağırsak hastalığı bulunan veya lif tükettiğinde şikâyetleri artan kişilerin beslenme değişikliğini hekim ya da diyetisyen desteğiyle planlaması önemlidir. Unutmayalım, sağlıklı beslenme tek bir öğünün ya da besinin başarısıyla değil, her gün tekrarlanan seçimlerle şekillenir. Lif de bu seçimlerin en değerli parçalarından biridir.</span></div></div><div class="Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__container Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__dirRow w-full Genellikle de dağılan yuvalardan insanın içinde hep bazı pişmanlıklar kalır. En çok da çocuklar söz konusu olduğunda. Belli bir yaşa gelene kadar da insan özellikle çocuklarına karşı sergilediği bazı tavırlar için hep kendini haklı çıkaracak sebepler bulur. Ama belli bir yaşa gelip artık hayatının olgunluk dönemine ulaştığında pişmanlıklarını itiraf edecek gücü kendinde bulur.EMEKLERİNİN TAÇLANDIĞI GECEDE GELEN İTİRAFBelli ki müzik dünyasının yaşayan efsanelerinden biri olan Phil Collins de tam böyle bir durumda. Müzik tarihine damgasını vuran Genesis grubunun üyelerinden olan 75 yaşındaki Collins, 2022'den bu yana yaşadığı sağlık sorunları yüzünden sahneye çıkamıyor.Bazı özel gecelerde sahnede boy gösterse de ya tekerlekli sandalyede oluyor ya da önceki gece olduğu gibi bastonuyla ayakta duruyor. Phil Collins, önceki gece de Rock'n Roll Hall of Fame törenine katıldı. O gece hem Collins'in müzik dünyasına katkıları kutlandı hem de ünlü sanatçı, belki de en kişisel itiraflarından birini yaptı. 'HAYATINIZI ZORLAŞTIRDIM... SİZİ ÖLÜMÜNE SEVİYORUM' Gecede Collins'e, çocuklarından biri hatta belki de en ünlü çocuğu, Emily in Paris dizisinin yıldızı olan kızı Lily Collins eşlik etti. Efsane müzisyen sahnede yaptığı teşekkür konuşmasında çocuklarına ayrı bir yer ayırdı. Tören boyunca ardı ardına duygusal anlar yaşayan Phil Collins çocukları hakkında konuşurken "Hepsi inanılmaz derecede yetenekli. Büyürken hayatlarını biraz zorlaştırmış olabilirim. Onları seviyorum" dedi Sonra da beş çocuğuna "Sizi ölümüne seviyorum" diye seslendi. Phil Collins'in üç farklı evliliğinden beş çocuğu bulunuyor. ÇOCUKLARI BAŞ UCUNDA TOPLANIP ONA VEDA BİLE ETTİ Genesis grubunun bateristi olarak müzik dünyasına adını yazdıran Phil Collins, daha sonra kariyerine solo olarak devam etti. Baterist, şarkı sözü yazarı ve solist olan Phil Collins, sağlığını büyük oranda geçmişte yaşadığı kötü alışkanlıkları yüzünden yitirdi. Hatta bundan iki yıl önce durumu gerçekten ciddileşti ve kendi deyimiyle ölüm döşeğine yattı.Genesis grubunun bateristi olarak ünlenen Phil Collins'in sağlığı, büyük oranda kötü alışkanlıkları yüzünden bozuldu. İki yıl önce de ölümden döndü. Organ yetmezliği nedeniyle İsviçre'de bir klinikte tedavi gördü Collins. O kendini bilmez halde yatarken ve bütün çocukları başına toplanıp ona veda sözlerini söyledi. Ama sonra Collins toparlandı ve hayata döndü. Kendisi bütün bu olanların farkında bile değilken, çocukları onu kaybetme korkusuyla yüz yüze geldi.ÜÇ EVLİLİKTEN BEŞ ÇOCUK: Phil Collins, ilk evliliğini Andrea Bertorelli ile yaptı. Bu evliliğinden 53 yaşında Joely ve 49 yaşında Simon adında iki çocuğu oldu.Jill Tavelman ile evliliğinden de 37 yaşındaki oyuncu kızı Lily Collins dünyaya geldi.Collins, üçüncü evliliğini yaptığı Orianne Cevey'den 25 yaşında Nicholas ve 21 yaşında Mathew adında iki erkek evlat sahibi oldu. YANINDA 24 SAAT BİR HEMŞİRE VARUzun süredir sağlık sorunlarıyla boğuşan ve hareketliliği kısıtlanan Phil Collins, hastane deneyiminin ardından evinde yaşamaya başladı. Ama ünlü müzisyen öyle tek başına yaşayacak durumda da değil. Fox News Digital'e verdiği demeçte, bu yüzden de kendini işinin ehli bir hemşireye emanet ettiğini söyledi. Bu durumu "İlaçlarımı zamanında aldığımdan emin olmak için yanımda sürekli bir hemşire bulunuyor. Ayrıca bana her an destek olan bir asistanım da var" diyerek anlattı. Yine de öyle yapayalnız, acınacak bir durumda olmadığını sözlerine ekledi. Televizyonda belgesel izlediğini, haftada üç gün fizyoterapi gördüğünü belirtti.</span></div></div><div class="Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__container style="font-size:14px;line-height:18px;--typography-color:var(--secondaryDisabledText)">Alternative Medicine</span></div></div><div style="height: 114px;" class="Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__container w-full shrink-0 gap-12"><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-bold w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp:2;line-clamp:2;font-size:20px;line-height:28px;--typography-color:var(--smoke_coal)">Eataly istanbul’un ünlü İtalyan şefi Claudio Chinali: En sevdiğim yemek: Dünden kalma spagetti</span><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-regular w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp: 2; font-size: 15px; line-height: 23px; --typography-color: var(--primaryText);">İtalya’yı birleştiren Garibaldi döneminin komutanlarından General Enrico Cialdini’nin beşinci kuşak torunu… Napoli’de akademisyen bir ailede dünyaya geldi, mühendislik eğitimini yarıda bırakıp tutkusu mutfağın peşinden gitti. Michelin yıldızlı restoranlarda yetişti. 2009’da geldiği İstanbul’a âşık oldu ve bir daha ayrılmadı. Şehrin sevilen İtalyan şeflerinden, Eataly İstanbul’un direktörü Claudio Chinali ile bir araya geldik... İKİNCİ DÜNYA SAVAŞI ÇOCUKLARI Chinali, “Annem de babam da İkinci Dünya Savaşı sırasında doğmuşlar. Kültürel olarak zengin ama maddi olarak çok varlıklı olmayan bir ortamda yetiştim” diye anlatıyor: “Annemle babam 1970’te Roma’da tanışıp evleniyorlar. Annem o dönem uçuş görevlisi. Babam akademisyendi. Babamın işi sebebiyle uzun yıllar yurtdışında yaşıyorlar. İki ağbeyim Almanya’da doğuyor. Sonunda Napoli’ye yerleşiyorlar. Babam Napoli Üniversitesi Tıp Fakültesi’nde kimya ve biyoloji profesörü. Çok sayıda Nobelli çalışma arkadaşı var. Eve de misafir gelirlerdi. Çok kültürlü bir ortamda büyüdüm.” Claudio Chinali KADEMİSYEN AİLEMİN ŞEFLİĞE İYİ BAKMAYACAĞINI DÜŞÜNDÜM Sene 2025 Chinali’nin mutfağa ilgisi çocuk yaşta başlamış: “Evde annem karın doyurmak, babam tutku için yemek yapardı. Ben de mutfakta olmayı ve güzel yemekler yemeyi severdim. Bizim aile kuzeyli olduğu için evde geleneksel kuzey yemekleri yapılırdı: risotto, ravioli, polenta, bonfile, tagliatelle yenirdi. 15 yaşında annem beni bir yaz kampına yolladı. Teknolojiden uzak üç ay geçirdim. O kadar hoşuma gitti ki sonraki beş yıl gönüllü olarak her yaz bu kampta çalışmaya başladım. Mutfakla aşinalığım ve yemek konusunda çalışmak fikri aklıma ilk o zaman girdi ama akademisyen bir ailenin çocuğu olarak ailemin benim şeflik kariyerime iyi bakmayacağını düşündüm. Babam profesördü, bir ağabeyim Cambridge Üniversitesi’nde çalışıyordu, diğeri tıp fakültesini bitirmiş kardiyolog olmuştu. Onlardan sonra benim aşçılık okumam? Olamazdı (gülüyor)!” MUTFAĞIN DERİN SIRLARINI ÖĞRENDİM Şeflik tutkusunu içine gömüp Napoli’de telekomünikasyon mühendisliği eğitimi almaya başlıyor. Ancak: “Çok mutsuz oldum ve ciddi panik ataklar geçirmeye başladım. Sonunda ağabeyimin yanına Almanya’ya gittim. Onun teşvikiyle aileme şeflik tutkumu açıkladım. Bana tepki göstereceklerini düşünürken, ‘Tabii, istiyorsan neden olmasın?’ dediler. Bu, beni mutlu etmekten çok daha fazla strese soktu çünkü gözümde şeflikle aramdaki tek engel ailemdi. Bu engel kalkmıştı. Napoli’de bir bistro-barın mutfağında işe başladım. Bir yıl burada salatlar, sandviçler yaptım. O sırada meşhur İtalyan şef, iki profesyonel babamdan biri olan Igles Corelli ile konuşuyordum. 2006 yılında onun Michelin yıldızlı restoranında çalışmaya başladım. Ücret almadan 16 saate yakın çalışıyordum; bulaşıkları da yıkıyordum yerleri de siliyordum, her işi yaptım. Ondan mutfağın en derin değerini öğrendim; malzemeyi, tekniği. Onun ekibinden Michelin yıldızlı en az 20 şef yetişti...” Zeynep Bilgehan - Claudio Chinali İSTANBUL’A GELDİM VE ÂŞIK OLDUM Sene 1986 - Napoli Chinali, “Verona’da iki yıl çalıştım. 2008’de ‘En iyi genç şef ödülü’ aldım. Londra’da Gordon Ramsey’in mutfağı için teklif aldım ama elektrik alamadığımdan onu istemedim. 2009’da Michelin yıldızlı Bruno Barbieri özel bir yemek organizasyonu için İstanbul’a geliyordu. Ona eşlik etmek üzere ilk defa İstanbul’a geldim ve şehre âşık oldum! Herkes yeni gastronomi trendleri için ya Fransa, İngiltere, İspanya’ya ya da minimalizm görmek için Japonya’ya gidiyordu. Ben kendimi farklılaştırmak için Türkiye’ye gelmeye karar verdim. Birkaç sene zengin, çok kültürlü gastronomiyi, mutfağı öğrenir sonra dönerim diyordum; 16 yıldır buradayım (gülüyor)!” 2009’da Michelin yıldızlı Bruno Barbieri özel bir yemek organizasyonu için İstanbul’a geliyordu. Ona eşlik etmek üzere ilk defa İstanbul’a geldim ve şehre âşık oldum! Herkes yeni gastronomi trendleri için ya Fransa, İngiltere, İspanya’ya ya da minimalizm görmek için Japonya’ya gidiyordu. Ben kendimi farklılaştırmak için Türkiye’ye gelmeye karar verdim. Birkaç sene zengin, çok kültürlü gastronomiyi, mutfağı öğrenir sonra dönerim diyordum; 16 yıldır buradayım (gülüyor)!” Sene 1983 RASİM ÖZKANCA’DAN ÖĞRENDİKLERİM Sene 1997 Türkiye’de en çok şey öğrendiği isim Borsa Restoranları’nın sahibi rahmetli Rasim Özkanca olmuş: “Onunla üç yıl çalıştım. Rasim Bey’e göre güçlü uluslararası şeflerden oluşan bir grup geleneksel Türk mutfağını da geliştirmeye yardım edebilirdi. Bizi zeytinyağlılar, tandırlar, su böreklerine, gelenek tariflerine saygı duyarak, yeni yaklaşımlar getirmeye teşvik ederdi. 2012’de Eataly İstanbul için teklif geldi. 2022 yılından beri Eataly İstanbul’un Genel Direktörü ve bünyesindeki Terrazza Italia restoranının Executive Chef’iyim.” CHINALI’NİN İSTANBUL’U Chinali, 16 yıldır İstanbullu: “İstanbul’un en sevdiğim yönlerinden biri çok demokratik bir şehir olması; her cep için bir yer var. İstersen yatınla Boğaz’da turlarsın, istersen Ortaköy ve Etiler’de modern Türkiye’yi görürsün... Fatih’e gidersin, oradan Kadıköy’e; hepsi bambaşka tarzlar. Bütün kaosu içinde vapura binersin ve büyülü bir 20 dakika geçirirsin... Benim için İstanbul’da en büyülü anları geçirdiğim yer vapur; tüm kaos durur ve çeşit çeşit fikir üretebilirsin.” EN ÖNEMLİ KRİTER: İYİ ÇAY Gastronomik olarak Türkiye’de neler tercih ediliyor? Yanıtı: “Türkler yeniliğe çok açık değil ama sevdikleri zaman da tutkuyla tam seviyorlar! İyi yemek için para harcamaktan çekinmiyor ama parasının karşılığını her zaman almak istiyorlar. Restoranda kendisini iyi hissetmek de istiyor. Nereye gidilirse gidilsin, en önemli şey, çay! En iyi restoranda bile ‘kötü çay’ çok kötü bir etiket.” ANANASLI KÜFLÜ PEYNİRLİ PİZZA Chinali sert bir şef değilmiş: “Bana ‘Ananaslı pizza dersen’; ananası bir malzeme olarak değerlendirir, onunla uyumlu ve lezzetli bir kombinasyon yaratmak için çalışırım. İtalyan küflü peynirlerinden biriyle, ananaslı chutney’i bir araya getirerek çok ilginç bir pizza ortaya çıkarabilirim. Önemli olan malzemelere ve lezzet dengesine saygı göstererek yenilik yaratabilmek.” İtalyan mutfağı tüm dünyada olduğu gibi Türkiye’de de popüler. Bunun sebebi: “Kaliteli malzemelere dayanması, sade hazırlanması ve doğal lezzetlere saygı gösterilmesi. Dünyadaki herkes 1980’lerin İtalyan yemeklerini seviyor. O zaman İtalyan ekonomisi çok iyiydi, turist çoktu ve büyülü bir andı. Herkes o andan bir şey istiyor çünkü insanlara mutluluğu hatırlatıyor; panna cotta, tiramisu, mantarlı risotto. Bunların hepsi 1980’lerde meşhur oldu.” İYİ YEMEK İNSANLARI MUTLU EDER “Yemeği sevdiğim için yemek yapmayı da seviyordum. İyi yemek insanları mutlu eder. Dünden kalma spagetti en sevdiğim yemek! Babam sabahları bir önceki günden kalan makarnayı ısıtıp bana verirdi. Bu anı çok güzel.” KUZU TANDIR FAVORİM “En sevdiğim Türk yemeği Fatih’te yapılan tandır kuzu. Mumbar severim. İç pilav... Tatlı olarak da kazandibi!”</span></div></div><div class="Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__container Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__dirRow w-full items-center gap-20"><div shrink-0 gap-12"><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-bold w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp:2;line-clamp:2;font-size:20px;line-height:28px;--typography-color:var(--smoke_coal)">AI Entry-Level Jobs: Report Finds 1.5M Missing White-Collar Roles</span><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-regular w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp: 2; font-size: 15px; line-height: 23px; --typography-color: var(--primaryText);">Nov. 25, 2026 AI Entry-Level Jobs: Report Finds 1.5M Missing White-Collar Roles Industries that use AI the most are hiring fewer beginners, according to a new report from the Burning Glass Institute and RAISE US released on Monday. The report, called "Fewer Rungs, New Bridges," finds that white-collar industries now employ about 1.5 million fewer people than pre-pandemic trends would predict. But the story is not mass layoffs. In the authors' words, the missing workers "aren't being laid off; they're simply not being hired in the first place." What the report found about entry-level hiring The researchers looked at finance, insurance, information and professional services. Together these sectors employed 31.9 million people in August 2026, about 1.5 million short of where their growth from 2005 to 2019 would have put them. Hiring has slowed in these industries even as their output keeps growing. In the most AI-intensive industries, the share of job postings open to people with three years of experience or less was 3% to 8% below its 2021-2026 average in the year ending June 2026. Across the wider economy, that share barely moved. The authors are careful about cause. The 1.5 million figure is a net number that also reflects other forces, such as offshoring and older technology. They treat AI as one of several likely factors, not the only one. Which jobs are shrinking, and which are growing? The split is the most useful part of the report. Between 2023 and 2025, occupations most at risk of automation lost about 820,000 jobs. Over the same period, occupations where AI helps workers do more gained about 1.4 million. Office and administrative support took the biggest hit, along with clerical and customer service roles. Workers without a four-year degree are the most exposed. They hold 80% of the jobs most likely to be automated, compared with 64% of all jobs. And most proven paths from no-degree jobs into better-paid careers still end in roles that usually require a degree. Gina Raimondo, former U.S. Commerce Secretary and co-chair and CEO of RAISE US, called the findings a wake-up call for leaders "from Washington to Silicon Valley." What this means if you're looking for your first job The report's message for job seekers is that the old route, where you learn on the job in a junior role, is getting harder to find. The answer is to bring some of that experience with you. The report points to a few ways to do that: Get real-world experience early. Co-ops, apprenticeships and employer-designed projects can stand in for the training junior jobs used to provide. Learn to use AI on the job. The report urges more focus on applied AI skills, since roles where AI assists workers are the ones growing. Build the human skills. The researchers say communication and collaboration are becoming core skills across the economy, and they help people move into a wider range of jobs. There is some good news for career changers. Looking at 2,741 moves into jobs that employers struggle to fill, the researchers found AI could help newcomers close about 31% of the skills gap. In those cases, AI can work as a bridge into a new field rather than a barrier. Why employers should pay attention Fewer junior hires today means fewer experienced workers and future managers later. If AI takes over the tasks that once trained new staff, companies will need to find other ways to grow their own talent, through apprenticeships, rotations or structured projects. The report adds to a growing body of research on AI and early careers, including a Business Roundtable and Burning Glass briefing published in September. The next official signal is the November jobs report from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, due in early December. Watch for hiring trends in finance, professional services and office support roles.</span></div></div><div class="Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__container w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp:2;line-clamp:2;font-size:20px;line-height:28px;--typography-color:var(--smoke_coal)">Thanksgiving Travel 2026: Fewer Travelers as Costs Climb</span><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-regular w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp: 2; font-size: 15px; line-height: 23px; --typography-color: var(--primaryText);">Thanksgiving Travel Just Broke Its Record Streak. Blame Your Airfare Nov. 24, 2026 AAA expects 81.5 million Americans to travel at least 50 miles from home between today, Tuesday, Nov. 24, and Monday, Nov. 30. That's about 121,000 fewer people than last year, a 0.1% dip that ends three straight years of record Thanksgiving travel. Why are fewer people traveling this year? Cost is the main reason. AAA says higher travel costs partly explain the drop, and the numbers back that up. Domestic round-trip airfare booked through AAA averages $800, up 17% from last year. Gas is the other pressure point. AAA says August, September and October each set monthly records at the pump this year. If prices hold, this Thanksgiving Day could beat the holiday's previous record of $3.58 a gallon, set in 2022. Still, AAA says you won't feel much relief on the roads or at the airport, because volumes are still close to record levels. How are people getting there? Driving: 72.9 million, down from 73.1 million, or nearly 90% of travelers Flying: 5.96 million domestic flyers, down 0.2% Bus, train and cruise: 2.6 million, up 4.1%, the only group still growing Florida is the top domestic destination for AAA travelers. Detroit and Dallas made the top 10, both hosting Thanksgiving Day football games. When is the worst time to drive? AAA and transportation data firm INRIX say afternoons and early evenings will be the worst, especially around big metros like New York, Washington, Los Angeles and Boston. Today (Tuesday):worst 2 p.m. to 8 p.m.; best before 1 p.m. Wednesday: worst noon to 7 p.m.; best before noon INRIX also expects the Sunday and Monday after the holiday to be among the busiest days on the road. The return trip is the next crunch. If you're driving home, plan around Sunday, Nov. 29, and Monday, Nov. 30, and check AAA's local forecasts for your route before you leave.</span></div></div><div w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp:2;line-clamp:2;font-size:20px;line-height:28px;--typography-color:var(--smoke_coal)">NFL Thanksgiving 2026: How to Watch All 5 Games</span><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-regular w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp: 2; font-size: 15px; line-height: 23px; --typography-color: var(--primaryText);">The NFL's First Thanksgiving Eve Game Is on Netflix. Nov. 24, 2026 The NFL's Thanksgiving week runs five games over three days this year, starting with the league's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game on Wednesday and ending with a Black Friday matchup. You'll need Netflix and Prime Video for two of them. The other three air on regular broadcast TV. What is the NFL Thanksgiving schedule for 2026? Wednesday, Nov. 25: Packers at Rams, 8 p.m. ET, Netflix Thursday, Nov. 26: Bears at Lions, 1 p.m. ET, CBS and Paramount+ Thursday, Nov. 26:Eagles at Cowboys, 4:30 p.m. ET, FOX and FOX One Thursday, Nov. 26:Chiefs at Bills, 8:20 p.m. ET, NBC and Peacock Friday, Nov. 27: Broncos at Steelers, 3 p.m. ET, Prime Video The Rams host the Packers at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles to open the week. Which games can you watch for free? All three Thursday games air on broadcast networks: CBS, FOX and NBC. If you have an antenna or a cable package with your local channels, you can watch the full tripleheader without another subscription. If you've cut the cord, each Thursday game also streams on that network's service: Paramount+ for CBS, FOX One for FOX and Peacock for NBC. Do you need Netflix and Prime Video? Yes, for two games. Wednesday's Packers-Rams game streams on Netflix, and Friday's Broncos-Steelers game streams on Prime Video. Neither airs on broadcast TV nationally, so an antenna won't help. That means watching all five games takes up to five services, or two streaming subscriptions plus an antenna. Check current plan prices before you sign up, since some streaming tiers include ads. Why is there a Wednesday game this year? The Lions have hosted on Thanksgiving since 1934, and the Cowboys joined in 1966. A third Thursday game came in 2006, Black Friday was added in 2023, and 2026 adds Thanksgiving Eve, so it's the biggest holiday slate yet. Last year, the Packers beat the Lions 31-24, the Cowboys edged the Chiefs 31-28 and the Bengals beat the Ravens 32-14. After Friday, the NFL plays 10 games on Sunday, Nov. 29, and closes the week with Monday Night Football on Nov. 30.</span></div></div><div class="Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__container w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp:2;line-clamp:2;font-size:20px;line-height:28px;--typography-color:var(--smoke_coal)">Layoffs This Week (Nov 16-22, 2026): Yelp, Enphase, Westin</span><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-regular w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp: 2; font-size: 15px; line-height: 23px; --typography-color: var(--primaryText);">NEW YORK, Nov. 23, 2026 Layoffs This Week (Nov 16-22, 2026): Yelp, Enphase, Westin US employers filed 31 WARN layoff notices covering 3,251 workers between Nov. 16 and Nov. 19, according to tracker LaborCurrent. Two public companies, Yelp and Enphase Energy, also disclosed cuts in SEC filings, and both pointed to AI as part of the plan. Here's every major layoff we could confirm this week, based only on WARN filings and company statements. Which companies announced layoffs this week? Tech cuts are being tied to AI Yelp told employees on Nov. 18 that it is cutting nearly 5% of its full-time workforce. In its filing, the company said it plans to reinvest most of the savings, with a focus on AI-powered products. Enphase Energy, the solar equipment maker, is cutting about 12% of its workforce, or roughly 320 people. Its filing says it will move some work to lower-cost regions and use AI and automation to raise productivity. Most of the cuts should be done in the first half of 2027. Elsewhere in tech, Intel filed four notices covering 57 workers in Santa Clara, and data company Crunchbase filed for 67 job cuts in San Francisco. Plant closures hit hourly workers The biggest single notices came from outside tech. Dole Packaged Foods filed to close a California operation affecting 404 workers. Ideal Cabinetry in Florida, Morgan Truck Body in Ohio and Quad/Graphics in Wisconsin also filed notices tied to layoffs or closures. The largest notice of the week, 423 jobs at The Westin Seattle, is less bad than it looks. The hotel is changing management companies, and the filing says the new operator plans to offer jobs to almost all affected staff on similar terms. What the job data says Layoffs are still low by historical standards. New unemployment claims were 203,000 for the week ending Nov. 14. But the number of people still collecting benefits rose by 70,000 to 1.763 million, the biggest weekly jump since January 2024, which suggests laid-off workers are taking longer to find new jobs. If your company is on this list Check your WARN notice date. Under federal law, covered employers generally must give 60 days' notice before a mass layoff or closure. Ask HR about severance, health coverage and when your equity stops vesting before your last day. File for unemployment benefits as soon as your job ends, not when severance runs out, unless your state says otherwise. Several layoffs already announced take effect in early 2027, including Qualcomm's 517 California cuts, which were filed before this week..</span></div></div><div shrink-0 gap-12"><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-bold w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp:2;line-clamp:2;font-size:20px;line-height:28px;--typography-color:var(--smoke_coal)">Stock Market Crash? What the Correction Means for Your Job</span><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-regular w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp: 2; font-size: 15px; line-height: 23px; --typography-color: var(--primaryText);">NEW YORK, Nov. 23, 2026 Stock Market Crash? What the Correction Means for Your Job US stocks head into Thanksgiving week in a correction. On Friday, the S&amp;P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39 and the Dow dropped 949.73 points to 48,147.33, leaving both more than 10% below their records. The Nasdaq Composite sank 5.3% and has now erased its gains for 2026. For most working Americans, the index level isn't the real question. The real question is whether this sell-off reaches their job, their next offer or their retirement savings. What happened to the stock market? AI and chip stocks drove the drop. Nvidia fell about 14% on Friday after Reuters reported that the SEC is examining the company's accounting, and the semiconductor index lost more than 10% in a single session. The S&amp;P 500 lost 8.6% for the week, its worst week since April 2025. The Nasdaq is about 18% below its record, close to the 20% line that defines a bear market. The VIX, Wall Street's fear gauge, closed near 36. Is the sell-off costing people their jobs? Not yet, at least not in the layoff numbers. New claims for unemployment benefits came in at 203,000 for the week ending Nov. 14, which is low by historical standards. The warning sign is elsewhere. The number of people still collecting benefits jumped by 70,000 to 1.763 million, the biggest weekly rise since January 2024. That suggests people who lose a job are taking longer to find a new one. Hiring was already slow before stocks fell. Employers are hiring at the slowest pace since 2013, according to Indeed Hiring Lab, based on September government data. Why a falling market can freeze hiring Companies don't need to lay people off to hurt job seekers. They can simply stop opening roles. A falling share price often pushes leadership to review budgets, and tech companies feel it most because stock grants are a big part of pay. Some cuts are already on the books. Upwork has expanded its restructuring to about 37% of its workforce, and Qualcomm filed notice of 517 layoffs in California. What about your 401(k)? A correction is not a crash. Since 1985, the Nasdaq Composite has closed 10% or more below its record about 25 times, and roughly one in three of those turned into a bear market, according to Trefis. If you contribute every paycheck, you are buying shares at lower prices right now. Selling after a big drop turns a paper loss into a real one. If you're close to retirement, this is a good week to review your mix of stocks and bonds with a financial adviser. This article is not financial advice. What workers can do right now - Update your resume and Lobox profile while you're still employed. - If you're job hunting, expect slower hiring processes, especially in tech and AI-related roles. - If an offer includes stock, value it at today's price, not last month's. US markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early on Friday. Investors will watch this week's jobless claims for any sign that the market's pain is spreading to the job market.</span></div></div><div class="Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__container w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp:2;line-clamp:2;font-size:20px;line-height:28px;--typography-color:var(--smoke_coal)">Kötülük ekseni mi yeni dünya düzeni mi</span><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-regular w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp: 2; font-size: 15px; line-height: 23px; --typography-color: var(--primaryText);">İDDİALI ve provokatif işleri seven The Economist dergisi son sayısında “kötülük ekseni” adını verdiği bir ittifakı duyurdu. Rusya, Çin, İran ve Kuzey Kore arasındaki ilişkiyi İkinci Dünya Savaşı öncesindeki Almanya, Japonya ve İtalya arasındaki ittifaka benzetti. Aslında bu yeni bir durum değil. Irak Savaşı’nın hemen öncesinde Amerikan yönetimi de Saddam rejimi, İran ve Kuzey Kore için “şer ekseni” tanımını kullanmıştı. Fakat yazının zamanlaması manidar. Trump, Putin ve Şi arasındaki sonuçsuz görüşmenin aksine yeni dünya düzeninde farklı bir noktaya odaklanıyor. Dergi, jeopolitikte asıl önemli gelişmenin Batı karşıtı bu dört rejim arasındaki işbirliğinin derinleşmesi olduğunu söylüyor. Uzun birkaç makaleden oluşan dosyayı kabaca özetleyecek olursak, şu iddialar öne çıkıyor: Günlük çıkarların ötesinde: Dört ülke arasındaki işbirliği, geçici çıkar birlikteliğinin çok ötesine geçti. Askeri, ekonomik ve diplomatik düzlemlerde sistematik bir ortaklığa dönüştü. Somut ürün Geran-4 dronu: Rus üretim altyapısı kullanılarak İran’ın tasarladığı bu dronda Çin motoru var ve işçilik Kuzey Kore’ye ait. Yaptırımlar işlevsizleşti: Ukrayna ve İran savaşlarındaki işbirliği Rusya’ya yaptırımları işlevsiz hale getirdi. Rusya’nın elindeki gölge filo 200’den 3000’e çıktı. Artık Çin-Rusya ticaretinin yüzde 95’i dolar dışı yöntemlerle yapılıyor. Nükleer denge tehdit altında: Rusya, Çin’in nükleer denizaltı ve füze uyarı sistemlerine yardım ediyor. Çin ve Rusya, Kuzey Kore’yi tam nükleer güç olma yolunda destekliyor. Rusya ve Kuzey Kore, İran’ın bölgesel çatışmada hayatta kalmasına katkı sağlıyor. Yeni Mihver İttifakı: Farklı coğrafyalarda çıkan çatışmalar Batı’nın çıkarlarını bölüp dikkatini dağıtırken bu dört devlete yarıyor. Aralarındaki ilişki 1930’lardaki Mihver Devletlerine benziyor Bütün bunların yanında Trump’ın NATO ve Avrupa’ya yönelik tutumunun da bu ittifakın elini kuvvetlendirdiği iddia ediliyor. Trump’ın en son “Ukrayna’ya yardımı kesin” çağrısı bunun kanıtı olabilir. Ancak günümüzde yaşanan dönüşümü bu dört ülke ittifakına indirgemek ya da yeni bir Doğu-Batı bloklaşmasıyla sınırlandırmak hata olur. Günümüzde asıl mesele, orta güçlerin çok boyutlu ittifak arayışında saklı. Diğer yanda İngiltere tekrar Avrupa Birliği ile yeni bir yol haritası oluşturmaya çalışıyor. AB, ekonomisini kurtarmak için Hindistan’a yanaşıyor. Bir tarafta İsrail, Yunanistan ve Hindistan’ı bir araya getiren, diğer tarafta Türkiye, Pakistan, Suudi Arabistan’ın öncülüğünü yaptığı yeni bölgesel ittifaklar var. Tüm bunların üstüne herkes kendi alanını ne pahasına olursa olsun korumaya çalışıyor. Mesela, AB’nin mültecileri Ruanda’ya sürme planı bunun bir tezahürü. Şurası gerçek ki dünya ABD ve Avrupa da dahil demokratik değerlerin ikincil plana itildiği, güvenlik kaygılarının depreştiği bir döneme girdi. Mesele “kötülük ekseni” değil. Herkesin kendi göbeğini kestiği bu dönemde artık kimse başkasının derdiyle ilgilenmek istemiyor. Tam da bu yüzden özellikle orta güçler arasında çok boyutlu ittifaklar görülüyor. SOYKIRIM KARARINDA İSRAİL MESAJI ULUSLARARASI Adalet Divanı, Myanmar kararıyla tarihinde ilk kez bir ülkenin soykırım yaptığına hükmetti. Önceki günkü karar aynı zamanda Soykırım Sözleşmesi’nin uygulanması ve İsrail hakkındaki dava bakımından önem taşıyor. Mahkeme kararında soykırım için kanıt eşiğini düşürmedi. Ancak hedef alınan nüfusun büyüklüğünü, hayatta kalanların uğradığı ruhsal zararı, çocukların öldürülmesi ve köylerin yıkılıp yerine yeni yerleşim inşa edilmesine özel atıfta bulundu. Bu yaklaşım Güney Afrika’nın İsrail’e karşı açtığı Gazze davasında da önem taşıyabilir. MYANMAR’daki katliam çok uzak tarihli değil. 2017’de etnik temizliğe dönüşen çatışmalar patlak verdiğinde bölgeye giden ilk basın kuruluşlarından biri Hürriyet’ti. İdris Emen, katliamdan kaçmaya çalışan on binlerce Arakanlı’nın Bangladeş sınırını geçmesine tanıklık etmiş, yaşanan dramın dünyada duyulmasına aracılık etmişti.</span></div></div><div w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp:2;line-clamp:2;font-size:20px;line-height:28px;--typography-color:var(--smoke_coal)">Central Florida Flooding: Timeline for Friday’s Heavy Rain</span><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-regular w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp: 2; font-size: 15px; line-height: 23px; --typography-color: var(--primaryText);">ORLANDO, Fla. | Nov. 20, 2026 Central Florida flooding is set to get worse Friday as another round of heavy rain moves over ground that is already soaked. Forecasters expect 4 to 8 more inches east of Orlando, with isolated totals above 10 inches, and the heaviest rain arriving Friday morning. The new rain lands on top of what fell from Tuesday through Thursday, when neighborhoods in Brevard and Volusia counties flooded and the St. Johns River broke a record that had stood since 1953. When will the heaviest rain hit? Rain was expected to build late Thursday night, peak Friday and taper off by early Saturday morning. The setup depends on a developing area of low pressure off the South Florida coast. If it tracks closer to Florida, rainfall totals go up. Forecasters at WKMG News 6 said the closer track is the more likely one. FOX 35 meteorologists put Brevard County at 8 to 16 inches through early Saturday, with 4 to 8 inches from New Smyrna Beach into eastern Orange and Osceola counties. Orlando and Sanford are looking at closer to 2 to 4 inches. The system could gain subtropical or tropical traits as it moves north Saturday. Drier weather is expected to return Sunday. Where is flooding worst right now? Brevard County has taken the hardest hit so far. FOX 35 reported more than 100 people rescued there and roughly 21 inches of rain in Melbourne Beach over two days. The American Red Cross opened a shelter in Melbourne. Seminole County has urged people in low-lying areas along the St. Johns River to leave if they can. Schools in Brevard, Volusia and Flagler counties canceled classes Friday. With the ground saturated, even a short burst of heavy rain can cause dangerous flash flooding. Flooded streets can stop even self-driving cars, as San Francisco saw this week when record rain swamped the city. Never drive through standing water, and check weather.gov for the latest National Weather Service alerts for your county. Why the St. Johns River will flood for weeks This is the part of the story that will outlast the storm. The St. Johns River near Cocoa has already passed its 1953 record of 17.6 feet and is still rising. The St. Johns is one of the slowest-flowing rivers in the country. Water drains north toward Jacksonville very slowly, so river levels downstream, near Lake Harney, Sanford and Astor, can keep rising for days after the rain stops. Seminole County Emergency Management has warned flooding could continue through December. That means homeowners along the river should plan for weeks of high water, not just a bad weekend. The heaviest rain falls Friday, with forecasters watching where the low-pressure system tracks. Rain should ease Saturday, then the focus shifts to the St. Johns River, where new crests are expected downstream in the coming days.</span></div></div><div shrink-0 gap-12"><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-bold w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp:2;line-clamp:2;font-size:20px;line-height:28px;--typography-color:var(--smoke_coal)">Jumbo Stay 747 Hotel Is Being Scrapped at Stockholm Arlanda</span><span class="index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__base index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__lineNumber index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__color index-module-scss-module__nlcBwa__font-regular w-full" style="-webkit-line-clamp: 2; font-size: 15px; line-height: 23px; --typography-color: var(--primaryText);">STOCKHOLM, Nov. 20, 2026 Jumbo Stay Hotel: Sweden's Famous 747 Hostel Is Being Scrapped The Boeing 747 that served as the Jumbo Stay hotel at Stockholm Arlanda Airport is being dismantled this month. Airport operator Swedavia started removing the jet in November 2026, about 20 months after the quirky hostel closed following bankruptcy. For 16 years, the jumbo jet was the first thing many travellers saw as they drove into Arlanda. Now it is disappearing piece by piece. What happened to the Jumbo Stay hotel? Jumbo Stay shut down in March 2025 after its operator went bankrupt, cancelling more than 800 upcoming bookings. No buyer or new operator came forward, and Swedavia, which owns the land, was left to deal with the aircraft. Swedish local paper Mitt i reported that crews had already removed the engines and cut off the wings. Contractors are now stripping the interior and separating hazardous materials before the fuselage itself is taken apart. Swedish media say the work should be finished by the end of the year. "It's time now," Arlanda airport director Karl Eklund told Swedish Radio's P4 Stockholm. He said the jet had been a good feature at the airport for many years, but recently it hadn't been what you want to see when passing by. Swedavia has not decided what the site will be used for next. The plane had a long life before it became a hotel This wasn't just any 747. The jet entered service with Singapore Airlines in 1976 and later flew for Pan Am, the most famous name in jumbo jet history. Its last operator was Transjet, a Swedish charter airline that went bankrupt in 2002, leaving the plane parked at Arlanda. Swedish entrepreneur Oscar Diös bought it and turned it into Jumbo Hostel, which opened in January 2009. The rebuild gave it 33 rooms and 76 beds. The most popular booking was the cockpit suite, where guests slept beneath the old flight deck windows. Diös told Swedish broadcaster SVT in April 2025 that he hoped the plane wouldn't be cut up for its aluminum. That is now what's happening. Why did Jumbo Stay fail? A novelty hostel had a hard time against large chain hotels. Swedish business outlet Realtid reported that big hotels built right next to Arlanda's terminals took business away from the much smaller Jumbo Stay. Once the hostel went bankrupt, the estate did not have the money to remove the aircraft, so the cost fell to Swedavia. Can you still sleep in a plane? Jumbo Stay was the only hostel you could book inside a real 747, and that option is now gone. Other airplane-themed stays exist around the world, but most use smaller aircraft. In Amsterdam, the Corendon hotel shows off a former KLM 747 on its grounds, but guests can't go inside. Dismantling is expected to wrap up by the end of 2026. After that, Swedavia will decide what to do with the land at the Arlanda entrance.</span></div></div><div class="Flex-component-module-scss-module__Lkixxa__container Answers vary a lot between employers.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2\u003eWhere do accountants work?\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003eAccountants work almost everywhere money moves. Is being an accountant stressful?\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eIt can be, mostly around deadlines. Month-end close, year-end and tax season bring pressure and sometimes long hours. What is the difference between an accountant and a CPA?\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eAn accountant is anyone working in accounting. A CPA is an accountant who has met their state's education and experience rules and passed the CPA exam. Get those right and your resume lands in the recruiter's queue looking the way you wrote it.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eBelow you'll find a free ATS-friendly resume template in Word, the formatting rules that matter, a filled example, and a two-minute test you can run on your current resume before you hit apply.\u003c/p\u003e\u003c/section\u003e\u003csection data-article-block=\"section\"\u003e\u003ch2\u003eWhat is an applicant tracking system resume?\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003eAn applicant tracking system (ATS) is the software employers use to collect applications, store candidate profiles and move people through hiring stages. An applicant tracking system resume is simply one the software can parse into the right fields (name, job titles, dates, skills) without scrambling the text, so a recruiter can find and read it.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe parsing part is the important bit. When you upload a file, the ATS pulls the text out and sorts it into a candidate record. If your layout confuses it, your job title might end up in the wrong field or your contact details might go missing. The recruiter then sees a messy profile, or doesn't find you in a keyword search at all.\u003c/p\u003e\u003c/section\u003e\u003csection data-article-block=\"section\"\u003e\u003ch2\u003eDo applicant tracking systems reject resumes automatically?\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003eMostly no. In an \u003ca href=\"https://enhancv.com/blog/does-ats-reject-resumes/\" target=\"_blank\"\u003eEnhancv study\u003c/a\u003e of 25 US recruiters (September to October 2025), 23 said their ATS does not auto-reject resumes. A person still makes the call. The automatic rejections that do happen usually come from knockout questions, such as work authorization, a required license or location.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eYou've probably seen the claim that 75% of resumes are rejected by software before a human looks at them. It gets repeated everywhere, usually with no study behind it. The recruiters in that study pointed to something more ordinary: volume. A popular role can attract far more applicants than anyone can read closely, so recruiters search and filter.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThat changes what you should focus on:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e• \u003cstrong\u003eReadability.\u003c/strong\u003e If the ATS parses your resume badly, a recruiter skimming the profile sees a mess.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e• \u003cstrong\u003eSearchability.\u003c/strong\u003e Recruiters search candidate databases by job title and skill. If your resume never uses the words they search for, you don't show up.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e• \u003cstrong\u003eKnockout questions.\u003c/strong\u003e Answer them honestly and carefully. A wrong click on \"Are you authorized to work in the US?\" does more damage than any font choice.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eSome ATS platforms also show AI match or fit scores. In the same study, 11 of the 25 recruiters had them, and most used the score as a guide rather than a decision.\u003c/p\u003e\u003c/section\u003e\u003csection data-article-block=\"section\"\u003e\u003ch2\u003eFree ATS-friendly resume template (Word)\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://docs.google.com/document/d/16IOju3PnStvSKa0vO3DTkY_rmPYA_8T2/edit?usp=sharing\u0026amp;ouid=105485731668541224164\u0026amp;rtpof=true\u0026amp;sd=true\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e[Download the free ATS-friendly resume template (.docx)]\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003c/section\u003e\u003csection data-article-block=\"section\"\u003e\u003cp\u003eThis template is built for parsing first and looks clean enough for the human who reads it next. It's a Word file, so it opens in Microsoft Word, Google Docs and LibreOffice.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eWhat's inside:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e• One column, no tables, text boxes, icons or graphics\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e• Contact details in the body of the page, not in the header\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e• Standard headings: Summary, Skills, Work Experience, Education, Certifications\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e• Word's built-in bullet points and heading styles\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e• Calibri 11 pt body text with simple bold for job titles\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e• Dates written the same way throughout (\"Mar 2024 - Present\")\u003c/p\u003e\u003c/section\u003e\u003csection data-article-block=\"section\"\u003e\u003cp\u003eHere's the structure, so you can see it before you download:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cblockquote\u003e\u003cp\u003e[FIRST NAME LAST NAME]\u003cbr /\u003e [Target Job Title, copied from the job post]\u003cbr /\u003e [City, State] | [Phone] | [email@example.com] | [Profile URL]\u003cbr /\u003e \u003cbr /\u003eSUMMARY\u003cbr /\u003e [Job title] with [X] years of experience in [2 to 3 core areas from the job post].\u003cbr /\u003e Known for [one specific strength backed by a result].\u003cbr /\u003e \u003cbr /\u003eSKILLS\u003cbr /\u003e [Hard skill 1], [Hard skill 2], [Software or tool], [Certification or method]\u003cbr /\u003e \u003cbr /\u003eWORK EXPERIENCE\u003cbr /\u003e [Job Title]\u003cbr /\u003e [Company Name] | [City, State or Remote] | [Mon YYYY] -
